issue.title: macOS rust-checks leg 6-10x slower than Linux and still growing
issue.description:
## Bug

- **Location:** `sase-core:.github/workflows/ci.yml` `rust-checks` (macos-latest leg)

The macOS `rust-checks` leg has grown 6-10x slower than Linux despite full rust-cache hits, and keeps growing. Successful-run durations over the last 400 CI runs (minutes):

| Period | p50 | p95 | max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| October | 27 | 36 | 41 |
| Nov 1-15 | 33 | 48 | 78 |
| Nov 16+ | 51 | 61 | 61 |

Linux stays at about 7 minutes. Queue time is only seconds to 5 minutes; the time is spent compiling the workspace crates. `sase_core` check takes 9m10s on macOS versus 59s on Linux, and the test-profile build takes 34m versus 4m. The release-cut wait-budget fix (130-min pass budget, 270-min merge job) papers over this but does not tune the leg.

Hypothesis to measure: memory pressure on the 3-vCPU / 7 GB arm64 runner when `--all-targets` compiles `sase_core`'s lib and lib-test concurrently. Possible levers: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, debuginfo level, and where clippy runs. Keep the macOS signal; the ci.yml cost note already says not to drop it.

task_type_fields.impact: Slow macOS pass starves the daily sase-core release cut and blocks the sase release train (core_cut_red, core_lag); the wait-budget fix only buys headroom.
task_type_fields.repro: Compare rust-checks durations: Linux ~7 min vs macOS p50 27 (Oct) -> 33 (Nov 1-15) -> 51 (Nov 16+); sase_core check 9m10s macOS vs 59s Linux with full cache hits.

issue.creation_reason: Release-cut timeouts were caused by the macOS CI leg outgrowing the merge budget; the budget fix lands separately and this tracks the underlying slowdown.
